correctness.rationale: Uniform k-tagged cycle sampling gives (n-1)! permutations per k. For i>=2, conjugation by adjacent-label transposition reverses a comparison except on two balanced exceptional events, so its conditional mean is 1/2. Explicit four-case sampling of Pi(1),Pi(2) gives the conditional first-descent law. Summation produces (n^2-3n+4)/(4n(n-1)) and the Eulerian variance gives correlation ~3 n^(-3/2). Boundary n=3 and k=n are included. Exact complete enumeration for n=3,...,9 and rational checks through 300 agree; the proof, not enumeration, supplies all-n validity.

originality.rationale: The selected 2005 first-image Eulerian refinement and 1989/1993 unmarked cycle-type/descent-set classification do not state the distinguished-cycle length profile. The existing fixed-point boundary and full-cycle marginal are acknowledged, not claimed as separate new findings. A matched type-and-descent-set counterpair at n=4 demonstrates that the unmarked type/descent statistic does not determine the distinguished length. The assessed new statement is the exact complete four-regime conditional local profile and its nonvanishing covariance, with a clear implicit-priority risk.

value.rationale: The marked-cycle length is a global orbit statistic while ordinary descents are order comparisons. Showing that conditioning on every possible cycle length leaves all positions after the first at their unconditioned expectation, with exactly four first-position regimes, is a structural classification of their dependence. It explains a positive limiting covariance 1/4 alongside correlation decaying at order n^(-3/2), and sharply separates first-image enumeration from first-orbit dependence. The all-dimensional finite law is mathematically motivated and not just a small-parameter computation.
